name: light-lattice
description: A lightweight lattice cryptography suite for digital signatures, key encapsulation, and authenticated key exchange.
intro: We bring together four algorithms for digital signatures, key encapsulation, and authenticated key exchange, exploring compact representations and efficient lattice-based constructions for post-quantum cryptography.

algorithms.name: BiT
algorithms.long_name: Bimodal Parabolic distribution based lattice signatures
algorithms.summary: Lattice signatures with parabolic masking and bimodal rejection sampling.
algorithms.intro: BiT is a lattice-based digital signature scheme built on the Fiat–Shamir with Aborts paradigm. It combines parabolic masking with a bimodal structure and a separately parameterized parabolic target distribution to improve rejection sampling.
features: Parabolic masking
Masking vectors follow a bounded parabolic distribution, concentrating probability near the center to strengthen masking.
Bimodal rejection
Rejection sampling uses a parabolic target distribution with a separately chosen radius to remove dependence on the secret key.
Compact representation
Public-key compression and signature hints reduce the amount of data that needs to be transmitted.

current.description: The BiT specification with parabolic masking and bimodal rejection sampling, including construction details, parameter choices, and security analysis.

implementation.description: Reference and optimized implementations of the BiT signature scheme.

current.description: Reference and AVX2 implementations of the BiT signature scheme with parabolic masking.

algorithms.name: ZEN
algorithms.long_name: Zero Divisor Encoding on NTRU Encryption
algorithms.summary: An NTRU-based KEM using zero-divisor encoding and a double-encoding framework.
algorithms.intro: ZEN is an NTRU-based key-encapsulation mechanism derived from DAWN. Its design combines zero-divisor encoding, double encoding, and polynomial-ring arithmetic to pursue compact ciphertexts and efficient computation.
features: Zero-divisor encoding
The encoding structure reduces noise amplification within the underlying NTRU encryption scheme.
Double encoding
A second encoding layer provides redundancy for correcting errors at the group level.
Efficient arithmetic
The design includes bit-based sampling and optimized polynomial inversion for constant-time implementations.

algorithms.name: PolarLAC
algorithms.summary: Module-LWE encryption and key encapsulation enhanced with polar codes.
algorithms.intro: PolarLAC combines Module-LWE with polar error-correcting codes. It provides public-key encryption and a CCA-secure KEM construction, bringing together small moduli, soft-information decoding, and spectral rejection sampling.
algorithms.design_focus: Small Moduli · Low Decryption Failure Rate
features: Small moduli
Most parameter sets in PolarLAC use q = 257, offering a favorable trade-off between security, bandwidth, and implementation efficiency.
Polar codes
Successive-cancellation decoding uses soft information about the noise distribution to recover the encoded message.
Spectral rejection
Sampling constrains the spectral norms of secret and noise polynomials to control decryption failures.

algorithms.name: CreTAKE
algorithms.summary: Two-message authenticated key exchange across KEM and signature credentials.
algorithms.intro: CreTAKE is a two-message authenticated key-exchange suite for endpoints with KEM-based or signature-based credentials. Four frameworks cover every ordered pairing of these credential types under a common interface.
features: Complete credential coverage
K2S, S2K, K2K, and S2S support both mixed and matching long-term credential types.
Two-message exchange
One message in each direction establishes a session key with authentication under the selected framework.
Concrete instantiations
The specification combines PolarLAC, ZEN, and BiT into 25 instances across three security levels.
